title: docs(site): ship the English deck 'The Ontology Is the Software' as a vector PDF under apps/docs/public/decks
body:
立卡门类别 ③ — 维护者直派的任务 (maintainer-directed task).

## Maintainer ruling (verbatim, untranslated)

> 是否建议这个PPT加一个英文版，放在官网上

> Jianguo Zhuang 是否建议改为 ObjectStack Team ，然后帮我导出pdf进仓库

Given in session https://claude.ai/code/session_011hRnra93sK5Q2gTYYTbdJR on 2026-10-08. The seat recommended the team byline (the blog essay and the context-window post are both bylined "ObjectStack Team"), and the maintainer's second line asks for the PDF to go into the repository.

## What lands

- `apps/docs/public/decks/the-ontology-is-the-software.pdf`: the English deck "The Ontology Is the Software — How a large model reads an enterprise", 17 pages at 1920 x 1080, printed by Chromium from the slide HTML (vector text, fonts embedded, about 770 KB). Byline "ObjectStack Team"; footer "The ontology is the software · objectstack.ai". It is served by the docs app at https://objectstack.ai/decks/the-ontology-is-the-software.pdf, the same way `apps/docs/public/hero-cover-dark.webp` is served at the site root.
- Nothing else. No page links to it yet: where it is linked from (the blog essay, a sequel essay, the README) is a separate maintainer decision still open in the session.

## Why this seat, not a dev dispatch

The PDF is printed from the deck artifact this session authored (https://claude.ai/artifact/WucbK5TnEDwXag5sNycoJc); a dispatched developer cannot reach the artifact, and the only work in the repository is adding one binary file. No code, no docs prose, no generated ledger changes.

## Guardrails

- One file, one binary, under `apps/docs/public/decks/`. No `packages/**`, no `content/**`, no `README.md`, no app code.
- Nothing publishes: `skip-changeset`.
- No model identifiers anywhere in the PDF, the commit or the PR.
- The seat never merges its own PR: the PR is left as a draft for the maintainer to land.

## Duplicate check (2026-10-08, open and closed)

- Query "English slide deck PDF the ontology is the software website apps/docs/public download": 3 hits — #22240 (the compare and when-to-use pages, in flight, different files), #21838 (the blog essay, closed), #21574 (positioning adoption, closed). None ships a deck or a PDF.
